problem: Searching the web for technical answers takes many steps.

founders.name: Michael Royzen
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page. Later founded Standard Signal.

exit.reason: Not stated by company in sources seen; aggregators credit competition from general model search.

technical_complexity.rationale: Training and serving LLMs and search with citations as a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Own models gave a brief edge but model labs shipped search.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Aggregators say general models added web search, eroding developer search.

market_need_then: Developers searched for code answers; the Feb 2023 Hacker News debut was received as a generative search engine for developers.

branding.name_origin: Rebranded from Hello to Phind in late Dec 2022; the Ph spelling reportedly suggested by Paul Graham as a play on find, per wiki summaries.
branding.domain_note: Bought phind.com from an older Canadian entrepreneur, per aiwiki summary.

rebrands.why: Domain brainstorming; sayhello.so domain judged weak

branding.community_and_virality: Open source coding models ranked #1 on Hugging Face in 2023 per YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable play on find with strong developer awareness but Ph spelling hurts typing; sources are wikis.

outcome_analysis: Phind built a developer AI search engine from YC S22, drew attention with open models in 2023, then raised a reported $10.4M in December 2025. It shut down on January 16 2026 per aggregators, weeks after raising. Aggregators attribute this to model labs adding search, which rests on commentary rather than a company statement.
notes: Shutdown date and Series A lead rest on aggregators (Everydev, Neuronfeed); Axios page returned 403 and only its snippet was seen. phind.com fetch was blocked. Series A label per Everydev.
